newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks slip despite industrial demand.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks slip despite industrial demand.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell on Wednesday in moderate trade dominated by large deals mainly focused on blue chip industrials, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index dropped 0.16 points to 153.16 points in turnover of 759,560 dinars ($932,118).
Jordan Hotel Tourism, unchanged at 8.25 dinars, was the heaviest trade stock with a single 247,500 dinars bloc transaction executed by one investor.
Brokers said activity was mostly block sales by large investors, some of whom are reported to be foreign bargain hunters.
Three industrials were the busiest traded stock: Electric Power, National Cable and Wire Manufacturing and Jordan Cement Factories.

The first two were unchanged at 1.59 dinars and 2.35 dinars. Jordan Cement, which has been a focus of large portfolio buying, rose a slight 0.01 dinars to 3.43 dinars in trade worth 104,203 dinars with 25,000 stocks bought by one investor.
But brokers said there were few fundamentals driving trade on another quiet day becalmed by the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
"The market was a continuation of the state of recession and minimal trade despite the large turnover which was mostly bloc sales," one broker said.
Irbid Electricity, which is expected to announce healthy 1996 results, was the top gainer with a 4.90 percent rise to 1.50 dinars, near the maximum five percent daily price swing.
A handful of mostly industrial firms led the remaining more modest rises, including Intermediate Petrochemical Industries, which rose 0.93 percent to 1.09 dinars.
Overall declining shares outnumbered gainers by 17 to nine, with shares in another 10 companies trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.12 percent to 81.46 points.
